headline: Sell the District, not 'Washington': go-go, the flag and Ward 8 turn the Dybantsa reset into DC's reason to rep.
thesis: DC fans rep the city before the team: the three-star flag, 202, wards and quadrants, go-go and Chocolate City outsell the Wizards wordmark, and the most loved uniform in years was the city-first cherry-blossom City Edition. A 17-65 season that ended in the No. 1 pick, AJ Dybantsa, Trae Young re-signed and Anthony Davis kept gives a battered, show-me fan base its first real reason in years to put the jersey back on. Nike wins by building on the District's own civic type system and its official music, co-made and paid with the Black DC and Prince George's County creators who own them, and launched from Ward 8, where the franchise already practices and the Goodman League plays. The constraints are real: Young is adidas, Under Armour owns Maryland, and statehood slogans, hardcore and anything Bullets-gun are off limits, so Nike's lane is the team, the courts, the schools and the city itself.

archetype.name: The Hometown Behind the Capital
archetype.description: A Black-built, DMV-wide fan base that has stayed loyal to the District and the 1978 banner more than to the modern Wizards, and wears DC civic symbols as identity. It commits to the team when the team speaks DC and shows up East of the River, not on the Mall.

pulse.teamMoment: Washington went from the NBA's worst record (17-65) to winning the lottery: No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa joins Trae Young (re-signed for about $212M over four years), Anthony Davis and young core Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George and Tre Johnson under Brian Keefe. There is no opening-night or Christmas game, so the first home marquee is the Oct 30 Cup Night against Charlotte in East Group C.
pulse.sentiment: Cautiously curious: real excitement about Dybantsa and the Young-Davis pairing, wrapped in gallows humor and a show-me demand for proof on health and fit before fans fully commit.

topInsights.title: The flag, 202 and the wards outsell the logo
topInsights.insight: Across every lens, locals wear the stars-and-bars, area codes, quadrants and ward numbers more readily than Wizards marks, and the 2022-23 cherry-blossom City Edition proved a city-first story sells. DC's civic type system (NW/NE/SE/SW suffixes, lettered streets with no J, 'Justitia Omnibus') is native, beloved and needs no license.
topInsights.implication: Make DC civic typography the house graphic language and let the Wizards mark ride second: small flag hits on jock tags and cuffs, quadrant-suffix numbering, one area-code lockup per jurisdiction with 202 as hero.

topInsights.title: Go-go is the law, and it was won in a protest
topInsights.insight: Go-go became DC's official music in 2020 after the 2019 #DontMuteDC fight at 7th and Florida in Shaw, so it reads as civic pride and an anti-displacement statement at once. It comes with a complete design system: Globe-style day-glo split-fountain posters, stacked wood type, the roll call, the PA tape and the conga-cowbell pocket.
topInsights.implication: Go-go is the market's richest untold uniform and product story, but only as a paid, credited co-creation with bands and Don't Mute DC organizers, launched in Shaw or Anacostia before any downtown theme night.

topInsights.title: Ward 8 is already the franchise's grassroots home
topInsights.insight: CareFirst Arena in Congress Heights holds the Wizards' practice court, the Capital City Go-Go and the Mystics, a short drive from Barry Farm, where the Goodman League made DC's Rucker and Durant and Wall played in 2011. The same corridor is go-go's heartland (Junkyard Band, Go-Go Museum & Cafe) and is underserved by retail.
topInsights.implication: Launch city product East of the River first, sell it on MLK Ave SE, and make the Goodman, Go-Go and Mystics one Ward 8 product line, so the rebuild visibly belongs to the fans who stayed through 17-65.

topInsights.title: The fan base lives in PG County and buys at DTLR
topInsights.insight: Chocolate City has largely moved to Prince George's County, and units move through DTLR, Foot Locker, the Mall at Prince George's, Tysons and Potomac Mills, while U Street, Shaw and Anacostia set taste and downtown serves tourists and gameday. Each ring reads the same logo differently.
topInsights.implication: Plan assortment by ring: Wizards name-and-number volume at the arena, Fanatics and DTLR; DC-identity and limited drops in community doors; area-code and county-specific product in PG and NoVA malls rather than one generic 'DMV' tee.

topInsights.title: A three-brand region: Nike's lane is team, courts and women
topInsights.insight: Trae Young is an adidas signature athlete and Baltimore's Under Armour dresses Maryland, while Nike's local assets are Kevin Durant's Seat Pleasant roots, Team Takeover on the EYBL, the Mystics' Nike uniforms and Jordan Brand's DC-born Kiki Rice. DMV hoopers claim pros by high school, county and area code.
topInsights.implication: Lead DMV product with the team, the Goodman, the WCAC and Interhigh schools and the women's game; use Young only through NBA-licensed team assets and build Dybantsa stories only once his deal is confirmed.

topInsights.title: The blossom is the tourist side of the line
topInsights.insight: The reported 2026-27 revival of the cherry-blossom City Edition lands on the March-April tourist peak, when visitors buy DC souvenirs rather than NBA gear, and locals separate the Mall's blossoms from their own city. They claim the later Kwanzan bloom at Hains Point and the Stumpy underdog tree as their own.
topInsights.implication: Sell the revived blossom kit at tourist price points downtown, but give locals a DC-artist-drawn 'Late Bloom' companion in Kwanzan pink and navy, and save the next new City Edition slot for go-go.

topInsights.title: Restraint is part of the design brief here
topInsights.insight: After the August 2025 federal police takeover, the 2025 job cuts and the 43-day shutdown, 'Free DC' and statehood slogans are residents' words, and federal-worker jokes sting. Nike's 2005 'Major Threat' poster still defines it for DC hardcore, and the Bullets name was retired over gun violence.
topInsights.implication: Use the flag and 'Justitia Omnibus' but never protest slogans, borrow nothing from hardcore, keep gun wordplay off everything, hold a visible entry price tier, and design an office-to-Metro layer for the fan coming straight from work.

opportunities.title: 'Tonight Only': the go-go poster system
opportunities.summary: A co-created go-go capsule that bills each marquee home game like a go-go show, built on the day-glo split-fountain poster, stacked wood type, PA tape J-cards and the roll call.

Songbyrd Music House and Som Records

opportunities.how: Co-design with Rare Essence or Backyard Band, Don't Mute DC and Long Live GoGo organizers and a Black DC poster artist, all paid and credited, with an original wood-type alphabet or MICA-printed Globe type. Open with a launch show at the Howard Theatre, acknowledge the 7th and Florida corner, and share revenue with go-go youth music programs.

collection.name: The District Pocket
collection.story: Washington's best product has always been the District's own: the beat that never stops, the flag on the forearm, the ward on the address and the warm-up found at the Eastern Market flea. The District Pocket sets the Dybantsa era to DC's official music and civic type, co-made and paid with the Black DC and PG County creators who keep them alive.

uniform.concept: The Pocket (go-go City Edition, for the next new City slot after the blossom revival)
uniform.narrative: Go-go is the beat that never stops, DC's official music since 2020, a status the city won by refusing to let a Shaw corner be muted. The Pocket dresses the team like the headliner on a day-glo flyer stapled to a Southeast utility pole, which every Black DC and PG County fan will recognize from a lifetime of shows. It is co-designed, credited and paid with go-go bands, Don't Mute DC organizers and a Black DC poster artist, and debuts at the Howard Theatre and in Anacostia before it reaches the court.
motifs: Split-fountain fluorescent gradient (yellow bleeding into pink) on the side panels
Concentric roto-tom rings as a tonal body emboss and the center-circle design
Roll-call text wall of the eight wards and quadrants, with no crew or block names
PA tape J-card with handwritten band, venue and date
uniform.typography: Chest wordmark 'DC' or 'THE DISTRICT' set as a stacked poster headline in an original condensed wood-type alphabet drawn by a DC letterer, or Globe type printed with MICA under license, never a stock font or traced archive poster. Numbers in heavy condensed gothic in poster-board white with a split-fountain inline.
details: Waistband: the eight-ward roll call, written with a working go-go lead talker
Jock tag: a PA tape J-card reading 'official music of the District, 2020' with the co-designers credited
Back neck: DC flag stars and bars at tattoo scale in Wizards red
Side panel: a split-fountain fade that runs yellow at the armpit to pink at the hem
Court: roto-tom ring center circle, day-glo baseline fade and the ward roll call along the sideline, with a live pocket band (congas, cowbell, roto-toms) at timeouts
avoid: Chuck Brown's name, likeness or 'Wind me up, Chuck!', band logos or reproduced historic posters without estate, band and MICA permission
Statehood or 'Free DC' slogans, BLM Plaza imagery or anything that turns displacement into nostalgia
Crew or block names in the roll call, and any bullet, target or gun wordplay
Hardcore and straight-edge references (the X, Dischord's look, Bad Brains' Capitol lightning)
A downtown-only 'go-go night' that launches without Shaw and East of the River partners and a revenue share

alternates.name: The Diamond
alternates.idea: The original ten-mile square tilted 45 degrees, with boundary-stone dot tape on the side panels, honoring Benjamin Banneker's 1791 survey for a Black History Month release.

alternates.name: Steamed
alternates.idea: A Chesapeake blue-crab gradient that runs from claw blue to cooked orange-red, echoing Wizards navy to red, for fall crab and R-month oyster season.

alternates.name: 1978 at 50 (Classic)
alternates.idea: Brief now for 2027-28: team-sanctioned 1970s red, white and blue stripes and block numerals for the title's 50th, with no gun imagery and only marks the team approves.

how: Lead with DC civic graphics and let the Wizards mark ride second on lifestyle product
Stage player depth in gates (first month, Feb 11 deadline, Play-In) rather than one big buy, given a health-dependent roster
Hold a visible three-tier ladder (entry tees and caps, core swingman and fleece, premium outerwear) for a market split between wealthy suburbs and price-sensitive neighborhoods
Launch every culture drop with paid, credited local partners in Shaw or East of the River before downtown or national channels

risks.risk: Brand conflicts: Trae Young is an adidas signature athlete, Under Armour dresses Maryland, and Dybantsa's and Davis's deals are unconfirmed.
risks.mitigation: Lead with team, league, school and city product, use Young only through NBA-licensed team assets, and build Dybantsa footwear stories only after his deal is verified.

risks.risk: Political flashpoint: after the 2025 federal police takeover, statehood and 'Free DC' messaging is partisan outside DC and shifts with each federal move.
risks.mitigation: Use the flag and 'Justitia Omnibus' only, keep protest slogans and BLM Plaza imagery off product, and check local sentiment right before each civic drop.

risks.risk: Extraction: go-go, Chocolate City and Southeast imagery sold downtown without Black DC creators reads as gentrification merch.
risks.mitigation: Co-design, credit and pay bands, organizers and ward artists, launch in Shaw and Anacostia first, and publish the revenue share.

risks.risk: A volatile roster: the playoff case depends on Davis's and Young's health and fit, and DC interest drops fast by March if the team slides.
risks.mitigation: Replenishment gates tied to the first month, the Feb 11 deadline and the Play-In; a playoff-push capsule held in reserve; DC-identity product that sells regardless of record.

risks.risk: A licensing minefield: the Bullets name (retired over gun violence), the Chuck Brown estate, MICA's Globe archive, WMATA, Ben's Chili Bowl, Georgetown, Howard and band marks, and Orientalism around the blossom.
risks.mitigation: Clear every third-party mark before design lock, keep gun imagery out entirely, draw original type and blossoms with DC artists, and keep blossom product botanical and DC-rooted.

scorecard.rationale: DC has one of the league's deepest and most ownable local cultures (an official music, a beloved civic flag and type system, Chocolate City and DMV hoops), and the Dybantsa reset makes this an above-average opening. Fandom sits below average after 17-65 and years of mediocrity in a hockey-first, visiting-fan-heavy arena, and retail is a wealthy but fragmented suburban mall-and-DTLR market with few DC-proper sneaker anchors.
